rationale: M14 IMPORTS_ENUM gap 1. `implements I<T>` published SOURCE TEXT as the edge endpoint and the production path then deleted the edge. The grammar puts a generic's type arguments in a SIBLING FIELD under `extends_clause` but NESTED inside a `generic_type` under `implements_clause`, and `extractClassHeritage` only skipped a `type_arguments` CHILD — correct for extends, never firing for implements. Measured on the pinned wasm: `extends B<T>` is `(extends_clause value: (identifier) type_arguments: (type_arguments ...))` and `implements I<T>` is `(implements_clause (generic_type name: (type_identifier) type_arguments: (type_arguments ...)))`. Corpus site: packages/typescript/src/api/node/node.generated.ts:41 (`class RemoteNodeList extends Array<RemoteNode> implements NodeArray<RemoteNode>`). WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT is the part this fixture exists to keep: the differential's normTarget strips type arguments on BOTH sides, so truth `implements:A->I` and analyzer `implements:A->I<T>` compared equal. A normaliser applied to both sides hides precisely the defect it normalises away. Corpus probe (script/m14/ts-construct-probe.ts): implements-parameterized 0 of 2 leaf-sites covered before the fix, 2 of 2 after. Every grammar shape is pinned, and so are the two ABSTENTIONS that keep the leaf rule from over-reaching: a predefined constraint names no symbol, and a type-parameter's own name is a binding.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAIN. Pre-fix this edge's target was the string "Shape<number>" — source text, an endpoint no consumer can navigate to — and pool-worker's angle-bracket filter deleted it before the index, so the production path published NOTHING here
one edge per parameterised interface on the clause, so this row appears TWICE with the same endpoints — two clauses, two facts
a QUALIFIED parameterised interface: the target is the LEAF (TSD4), not `Ns.Shape` and certainly not `Ns.Shape<number>`
the control: an unparameterized interface is unchanged
both clauses parameterised in one declaration
the extends arm already stripped correctly (sibling-field shape). Pinned so the two clauses cannot drift apart again
interface heritage with a parameterised base (extends_type_clause nests generic_type the way implements does)

M14 IMPORTS_ENUM gap 4: `<T extends Shape<number>>` names Shape, and the constraint was the ONLY place it was named. Pre-fix the pass emitted `references shrink -> T` (the binding) and nothing for the constraint

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT. A `type_arguments` sibling skip cannot catch this shape, so the whole generic_type text reached the target
the type ARGUMENT is not an implemented interface. Emitting it would be the `type_arguments` fabrication the extends branch's own comment warns about
heritage targets are LEAVES (TSD4/TSD3). A dotted target is an endpoint the leaf-identity contract exists to prevent
the extends arm's own regression: sibling-field shape plus the shared leaf rule
a PREDEFINED constraint names no project symbol — the same PRIMITIVES exclusion the declared-type pass already applies to a `const x: string`
the constraint's target is the leaf too; the reference pass reduces through the type node rather than taking raw text
every implements edge carries the interface NAME's line (M59.A7). The line belongs to the name, never to the construct that contains it
